name: The Keeling Curve
statement: A rising, saw-toothed record of atmospheric carbon dioxide, measured continuously since 1958.
meaning: The Keeling Curve is the graph of the continuous measurement of atmospheric carbon dioxide at the Mauna Loa Observatory in Hawaii since 1958, the longest continuous direct record of the gas in the world. It shows two things at once: a steady long-term rise in the background concentration, driven mainly by human burning of fossil fuels, and a regular annual saw-tooth oscillation, in which carbon dioxide falls through Northern Hemisphere spring and summer as growing plants take it up and rises again in autumn and winter as vegetation decays. It provided the first clear, direct evidence that human activity is raising atmospheric carbon dioxide.
mechanism: The record was made possible by careful, consistent instrumental measurement at a remote, high-altitude site. Mauna Loa was chosen because, far from cities, industry, and dense vegetation, its air is well-mixed background air representative of much of the Northern Hemisphere, with local volcanic and vegetation influences screened out. The annual saw-tooth is the breathing of the biosphere: because the Northern Hemisphere holds far more land and vegetation, its growing season dominates the global signal, drawing carbon dioxide down in spring and summer and releasing it in autumn and winter, a swing of a few parts per million around a relentlessly rising baseline.

examples.text: Carbon dioxide was about 316 parts per million when measurements began in 1958, against a pre-industrial level near 280, and it passed 400 in 2013 and has kept climbing since.
Each year the concentration dips in Northern Hemisphere spring and summer as plants photosynthesise and rises in autumn and winter as they decay, tracing the biosphere's annual breath.
Charles David Keeling began the measurements in 1958 and directed them until his death in 2005, after which his son Ralph Keeling took over their continuation at Scripps.

variants.name: The isotopic fingerprint
variants.text: The declining ratio of carbon-13 to carbon-12 in atmospheric carbon dioxide, which shows the added carbon comes from ancient plant-derived fossil fuels rather than from volcanoes or the ocean.

variants.name: The global network
variants.text: Independent stations from the South Pole to Barrow, and satellites, all showing the same rising trend, confirming that the single Mauna Loa record reflects a global change.

whyItMatters: It is a cornerstone of modern climate science, the clearest empirical evidence for the human-caused rise in atmospheric carbon dioxide, and it turned an abstract concern into a plainly visible upward curve. Sustained over more than sixty years by consistent, single-method measurement, it is also a model for long-term environmental monitoring, showing the scientific value of patient, uninterrupted observation, and its continuation from father to son embodies that commitment to an unbroken record.

working.text: read the annual saw-tooth as a natural seasonal cycle riding on a rising human-driven baseline, two independent features.
treat Mauna Loa's remote, high-altitude background air as a good proxy for the global trend, corroborated by the worldwide network.
use the declining carbon-13 ratio and falling atmospheric oxygen to tie the added carbon dioxide to fossil-fuel combustion.

limits: The curve measures concentration, not by itself the source of the added carbon dioxide, though the isotopic evidence of a declining carbon-13 ratio, and the parallel fall in atmospheric oxygen, do identify fossil-fuel combustion as the source. It is a single site, but it is corroborated by a global network, from the South Pole to Barrow, and by satellites, all showing the same trend. Its most recent value is a moving target, climbing a few parts per million each year, so any single current figure is quickly dated. Continuity has been preserved even through operational disruptions such as the 2022 Mauna Loa eruption.
misreadings: The annual wiggle does not prove the change is natural: it is a genuine seasonal cycle of plant photosynthesis and decay, but it oscillates around a relentlessly rising baseline, and the two features are independent, so the natural swing does not offset the human-driven rise. Volcanoes at Mauna Loa do not contaminate the data, since background-air screening removes local influence and the global network confirms the same trend at non-volcanic sites. And 400 parts per million was not crossed in one clean moment but at different times for daily, monthly, and annual means.
origin: Begun by Charles David Keeling of the Scripps Institution of Oceanography, who installed his carbon-dioxide analyser at Mauna Loa in 1958 during the International Geophysical Year and directed the record until 2005; it is continued by Ralph Keeling.

sources.text: Trends in Atmospheric Carbon Dioxide (Mauna Loa), NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory. — the continuous record, current values, and the 1959 annual mean.
The History of the Keeling Curve, Scripps Institution of Oceanography. — Keeling's 1958 start, the seasonal cycle, and the record's significance.
